examples.japanese: {舅|しゅうと}は{去年|きょねん}{亡|な}くなった。
examples.english: My father-in-law passed away last year.

examples.japanese: {舅|しゅうと}との{関係|かんけい}は{良好|りょうこう}だ。
examples.english: I have a good relationship with my father-in-law.

examples.japanese: {舅|しゅうと}と{姑|しゅうとめ}に{挨拶|あいさつ}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to greet my father-in-law and mother-in-law.

notes:
{舅|しゅうと} refers to the father of one's spouse. The kanji {舅|しゅうと} is rarely used in everyday writing; hiragana しゅうと is more common.

FORMALITY:
In formal or polite speech, {義父|ぎふ} or お{義父|とう}さん is preferred. {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち} (literally "father by obligation/marriage") is also used. {舅|しゅうと} itself has a slightly literary or traditional feel.

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- {姑|しゅうとめ}: mother-in-law
- {義父|ぎふ}: father-in-law (formal/written)
- {義母|ぎぼ}: mother-in-law (formal/written)
- {義理|ぎり}の{両親|りょうしん}: parents-in-law
- {嫁|よめ}: daughter-in-law, wife
- {婿|むこ}: son-in-law

CULTURAL NOTE:
Relationships with in-laws ({嫁姑|よめしゅうとめ}{関係|かんけい}) are a frequent topic in Japanese culture, especially the often-tense relationship between a wife and her mother-in-law.
